info.name: Workvivo Developers
info.description:
✨ Welcome to the Workvivo Developers site. ✨

On this site you will find our API documentation along with our Webhook documentation.

We love feedback

We are always trying to improve our API and developer offerings. If you have any feedback, please send us an email to api@workvivo.com.

request.description:
Notifications can be sent immediately or scheduled for the future. A notification with send_at in the future will be scheduled to send at that time. If send_at is in the past, it will send immediately. You can cancel sending a scheduled notification by deleting it. Note: the send_at date must be in ISO 8601 format.

Note: when sending notifications with audiences other than global, you must set the audience.type and provide an array of Workvivo Ids e.g.

{
    "audience": {
        "type": "spaces",
        "spaces": [1, 2, 3]
    }
}

Click on Global Audience above the example request on the right to see a different example.

item.description:
The Notifications API lets you send notifications to users. They will see these notifications in app and you also can optionally send email and/or push notifications.

Notifications can be sent immediately or scheduled for a date and time in the future.

Notifications can be targeted to everyone in your organisation, to members of particular spaces or teams, or to individual users by their Workvivo ids.

In certain cases, notifications will be throttled. For notifications with audiences larger than 10,000 people, there must be an interval of at least 5 minutes between any other notifications to the same audience.

item.description:
The SIEM API lets you query security related events associated with your users and Organisation.

Outlined below is a list of all possible events. Some events may not be possible for your Organisation's configuration. For example; your Organisation may have SAML authentication enabled, and so password reset events would not be generated.

Each Event includes:

  • created_at_timestamp
  • event
  • ip_address
  • user_agent
  • workvivo_id
  • user_email
  • note

Event - login

Indicates that the user_email logged into the Workvivo Application via password based authentication (NB SAML authentication has it own event).

Event - loginMobile

Indicates that the user_email logged into the Workvivo Application via password based authentication on a mobile device (NB SAML authentication has it own event).

Event - loginSaml

Indicates that the user_email logged into the Workvivo Application via SAML authentication.

Event - loginSamlFailed

Indicates that there was a failed SAML login attempt. The note attribute will include the impacted user's email address.

Event - loginSamlMobile

Indicates that the user_email logged into the Workvivo Application via SAML authentication on a mobile device.

Event - logout

Indicates that the user_email explicitly logged out of the Workvivo Application on a web browser.

Event - logoutMobile

Indicates that the user_email explicitly logged out of the Workvivo Application on a mobile device.

Event - MFA reset

Indicates that an administrator user (user_email) has reset an MFA token for a user. The user_email in the response indicates the the Administrator user performing the action. This event only applies if MFA is enabled for you native organisation. (this event does NOT relate to your IDP's MFA solution).

Event - User setup MFA successfully

Indicates that the user has setup MFA successfully, the user_email represents the user who has successfully completed MFA setup.

Event - user changed password

Indicates that the user has changed their password, the user_email represents the user who has successfully changed their password (not related to SAML, IDP, SSO enabled users etc.).

Event - password

Indicates that an administrator has updated a user's password. The user_id identifies the administration user who performed the action. The note attribute indicates the user impacted.

Event - password reset request successful

Indicates that the user has updated their password successfully. Only applies to password based authentication. Does NOT include SAML based authentication password changes.

Event - password reset request failure

Indicates that there was a password reset failure for a user. Typically suggests that an email address was used that does not exist. The user_email attribute highlights the email address used.

Event - switch user

Indicates that a user has switched accounts, i.e. delegated from one account to another and is now acting as that other user. The user_id represents the user switched into, while the real user is represented by real_user attribute.

Event - switch user reverted

Indicates that a user has switched back to their real user account. The real_user attribute represents the real user account, while the user_id represents the user switched into. This is just the reverse of the previous event.

Event - organisation

Indicates that a system setting has been changed. The user_email indicates who made the change. Changes such as default timezones, background images.

Event - App\\OrganisationSettings

Event - User Requested Report inactiveUsers

Event - Data Classification

Indicates that a user has added a data classification to an Update, Shout-out, Article, Page or Event.

request.description:
Mega Menu

This endpoint makes an HTTP GET request to retrieve the mega menu data.

Response

Upon a successful request, the server responds with a status code of 200 and a JSON object in the response body. The JSON object contains the following properties:

  • data (object) - Contains the mega menu data.

    • tabs (array) - An array of tabs within the mega menu.

      • title (string) - The title of the tab.

      • sorting_order (number) - The sorting order of the tab.

      • columns (array) - An array of columns within the tab.

        • items (array) - An array of items within the column.

          • title (string) - The title of the item.

          • item_type (string) - The type of the item (heading or link).

          • link_url (string) - The URL link associated with the item.

          • column_number (number) - The column number in which the item is placed.

          • sorting_order (number) - The sorting order of the item.

          • created_at (string) - The creation timestamp of the item.

          • updated_at (string) - The last update timestamp of the item.

      • published_at (string) - The timestamp when the tab was published.

  • status (string) - The status of the response.

  • meta (object) - Additional meta information related to the response.

Key Contacts

The key point of contact for your onboarding in the HR Team - they can be contacted through the HR Space in Workvivo or by emailing hr@example.com

\n

Building Access

item.description:
This documentation describes how to:

  • Use Workvivo APIs with a Bearer token.

  • Handle webhook requests from Workvivo.

  • Verify the authenticity of webhook requests using a JWT provided by Workvivo.

Authorization for Workvivo APIs

To interact with Workvivo APIs, you need a Bearer token for authorization. Include the token in the Authorization header when making requests.

Scopes Required

The following scopes are required to use Workvivo APIs for chatbot interactions:

  • chats.bots.read – For reading chatbot information and configuration.

  • chats.bots.write – For creating chatbots and updating the configuration of a chatbot.

  • chats.message.write - For creating messages in Workvivo chat.

Handling Webhook Requests from Workvivo

When a user interacts with a chatbot in Workvivo, Workvivo sends a POST request to the webhook URL specified during bot creation. This request includes a JWT in the x-workvivo-jwt header for verifying the request’s authenticity.

Webhook Request Format

  • HTTP Method: POST

  • Content Type: application/json

Webhook Header

x-workvivo-jwt: JWT generated by Workvivo

Example Webhook Payload
{
  "action": "chat_bot_message_sent",
  "message": {
    "message_type": "MESG",
    "bot_userid": "bot_user_id",
    "channel_url": "channel_url",
    "message": "test",
    "user_id": 3,
    "user_email": "ja@workvivo.com"
  }
}

Steps to Handle Webhook Requests

1. Verify the JWT:

Each webhook request includes a JWT in the x-workvivo-jwt header. This JWT is signed by Workvivo and must be verified to ensure the authenticity of the request.

2. Process the Payload:

After verifying the JWT, process the data payload based on the event type.

3. Respond to the Webhook:

Return an appropriate HTTP status code (e.g., 200 OK) after processing the request.

JWT Verification

The JWT generated by Workvivo includes a claim (publicKeyUrl) that specifies the host of the JSON Web Key Set (JWK). Use this host to fetch the JWK and verify the JWT.

JWT Claims

• aud: The host of the JWK for verification.

• exp: Expiry time of the JWT (ensure the token has not expired).

const jwt = require("jsonwebtoken");
const jwksClient = require("jwks-rsa");
const verifyWorkvivoRequest = async (token) => {
    const decodedToken = jwt.decode(token, { complete: true });
    const { kid } = decodedToken.header;
    const { publicKeyUrl } = decodedToken.payload;
    // Fetch the JWK
    const client = jwksClient({ jwksUri: publicKeyUrl });
    const key = await client.getSigningKey(kid);
    const signingKey = key.getPublicKey();
    // Verify the token
    return jwt.verify(token, signingKey);
};
// Example of verifying a JWT
const token = "<JWT-from-Authorization-header>";
try {
    const decoded = await verifyWorkvivoRequest(token);
    console.log("Valid request from Workvivo:", decoded);
} catch (error) {
    console.error("Invalid JWT:", error.message);
}

item.description:
Users One Time Passcode

One Time Passcodes are usually used in organisations where the employee does not have an email address. In these cases, an organisation will use a 3rd party Claim Portal. A Claim Portal is a standalone application that the organisation or Reseller Partner uses to provision unwired users with a username and password. This API is only available to vetted and approved Partners.

Support
Initial support for the use of the One Time Passcode API with a Claim Portal is limited is only available to vetted and approved Partners of Workvivo..

🔗 Fully working example implementations (Go, PHP, Python) are available on GitHub here

Before You Start

To facilitate the use of the API ensure the following requirements are met:

  • Authentication Mode: Must be 'mixed'.

  • Organisation Configured for One Time Passcodes: Ensure that the "Enable One Time Passcodes for Unwired Password Reset" parameter is enabled.

  • JWT Settings - JWKS URL: Ensure you have a valid JWKS URL configured in JWT Settings (either JWKS or JWKS-Hosted) - available in “API Keys & JWT Settings” in Workvivo Administration

  • App Setup with Permissions: Ensure you have created an App in Workvivo and assigned it the unwired.*.write permissions - available in “API Keys & JWT Settings” in Workvivo Administration

  • User Configured as Allowed One Time Passcodes: Ensure the relevant user is allowed to use One Time Passcodes (users.allow_otp_password_reset), visible in the Security Tab for the user in Workvivo Administration. Configured during User Provisioning / SCIM as outlined in the specification.

✅ You can validate all of the above checks automatically by clicking the "Validate" button in the "Apps and App Settings" section of Workvivo Administration on Apps with the unwired.*.write permission.

  • 📄 Original API spec and example: View the document

  • ❓ FAQ section: Go to FAQ

Required Headers

Headers for the One Time Passcode endpoint differ from other APIs. It is not possible to use the Authorization Bearer token as done with other APIs. Instead, the following two headers are required:

  • Workvivo-Id: Your Workvivo Organisation ID. You can find this in Workvivo in Apps Settings

  • x-workvivo-jwt: Your generated JWT. More details about this are included in the document linked to above or as below in the POST details.

  • Accept: application/json: This explicitly tells the API that your client expects a JSON response, ensuring consistent behavior across environments and avoiding default fallbacks.

More details of JWTs for Customer APIs can be viewed here.

Important Notes

  • Permissions

    • The roles Developer and IT Administrator are required to configure JWT SSO settings

    • The App created in Workvivo to perform this One Time Password API call must be granted the unwiredotp.*.write permission in Workvivo as outlined in the FAQ

item.description:
Base Url

You can find your Base URL when creating your Access Token in Apps and App Settings.

Required Headers

These headers are required for all requests:

  • Workvivo-Id: Your Workvivo Organisation Id. You can find this when creating your Access Token.

  • Accept: Must always be application/json.

  • Authorization: In the format Bearer {your-token-here}. See how to get an Access Token below.

For requests with a JSON payload they must also have:

  • Content-Type: application/json

​

Pagination

Every endpoint which returns a collection is paginated. You can include skip and take query parameters to determine which items you fetch. If you omit these parameters you will get the first "page" of data with a skip of 0 and the default value for take.

​

Query Parameters

Query parameters which take an array of items must be pipe-delimited e.g. teams=1|2|3

​

Get an Access Token

Note: to create an app and generate an access token you must have the Developer role.

⚠️ Warning: Granting a user the Developer role allows them to create API Apps. Those Apps can be given permissions, up to and including Admin permissions so make sure you trust a user before granting them this role. Please be aware that developers may have the ability to perform actions through the Customer API that your organisation restricts in the user interface.

  1. Navigate to https://workvivo.com/admin/developers/apps/manage

  2. Take note of your Organisation Id. You will need to pass this as a Workvivo-Id header for all requests.

  3. Create a new app. Select which permissions your app needs. You can change this later. We recommend only giving the minimum set of permissions needed.

  4. Click on Manage Keys for your App. Create a new API key and copy the Token.

  5. Paste your Token into your Authorization header. Don't forget to include Bearer before the token in the header.

For Legacy API docs please click here.

item.description:
Our API can be used to send data to Workvivo or request data from Workvivo. We also offer Webhooks where we will send POST requests when certain events happen.

Note: You will need to contact us to get Webhooks enabled for your organisation.

Configuring Webhooks

We offer a self-serve portal for managing your webhooks. Log in to your Workvivo account and go to Admin > Administration > Webhook Settings. Note: you will need the Developer role in order to manage webhooks and view logs.

From the self-serve portal you will be able to manage webhooks and also view logs of invocations within the last 30 days for the purposes of monitoring and debugging.

Webhook Scopes

When configuring a webhook under the Subscribed Events section you are able to choose whether you want to receive webhooks only for public content, or for all content. Note if you choose all content you will receive content from private & hidden spaces among other limited audiences. This may end up sending sensitve information to the webhook endpoint which you did not intend. Please consider carefully when selecting this option.

Note: Chat webhooks are never considered public so in order to receive chat webhooks you will have to have selected to receive webhooks for all content.

Delivering Webhooks

Timeouts

We have a connection timeout of 5 seconds and a response timeout of 5 seconds when sending webhooks. Please make sure your server can be connected to and responds within that timeframe otherwise we will stop waiting for the response and mark the attempt as failed.

Retries

When attempting to deliver a webhook, we expect a 2xx response code. If we do not receive a 2xx response code we will attempt redelivery up to 4 additional times (for a total of 5 attempts) with an exponential delay between subsequent retries.

Delivery Order

Webooks may not always be delivered in the order in which they were triggered. For example you may receive an article.published webhook just before you receive the article.created webhook for that same article.

Webhook Payload

All webhook payloads have the following common keys:

  • action - e.g. comment.created, article.published etc

  • meta - an object with:

    • id - a unique ID for this invocation of the webhook. If the webhook delivery is re-attempted, this id will remain the same

    • attempt - which attempt this is is deliver the webhook. Starts at 1.

    • timestamp - a Unix timestamp when we sent the webhook

In addition, webhooks have details related to the triggering event. For example, the article.created webhook will include an article key with an containing details of the article which was created.

Authentication

You can configure a webhook to be sent with no authentication. We also support OAuth 2.0 authentication. When configuring a webhook you can select OAuth 2.0 for the auth type and provide an OAuth 2.0-compliant Login URL along with a client id and secret. When sending webhooks we will generate an access token and append that as a Bearer token to the webhook requests via the Authorization header.

item.name: JWT SSO

request.description:
Below outlines the JWT claims (attributes), see example JWT here

  • iss (issuer)

    • issuer, this will be the customer’s host typically, e.g. acme.com

    • mandatory

  • sub (subject)

    • identifies the user, typically email address or some other unique identifier

    • mandatory

  • aud (audience)

    • should be the customer’s Workvivo registered domain, e.g. acme.workvivo.com

    • mandatory

  • iat (issued at)

    • epoch time that the token was issued at

      • e.g. 1669644000 // 28th November @ 14:00:00

    • mandatory

  • nbf (not before)

    • epoch time that the token should not be valid before

      • e.g. 1669644000 // 28th November @ 14:00:00

    • mandatory

  • exp (expires at)

    • epoch time that the token should be considered expired

      • e.g. 1669644015 // 28th November @ 14:00:15

    • value should be as short as possible, typically should not be > 15 seconds.

    • mandatory

  • state

    • mandatory by default, though can be disabled using the optional disableState attribute.

    • used to prevent replay attacks

    • it is not recommended to disable this attribute

    • this should be a secure random string acting as a nonce

    • this is a secure random string acting as a nonce

    • by default the JWT can only be used once based on the state value

    • mandatory (unless disabled via disableState attribute)

  • disableState

    • by default the JWT can only be used once based on the state value

    • you may disable this, by setting disableState to true, it is not recommended to disable state

    • you do not have to set disableState to false, its assumed to be false

    • optional

  • organisation_id

    • used as part of validation for tenancy

    • this organisation ID is verified against the organisation ID associated with the 'aud' attribute

    • mandatory

  • redirectURL

    • this is the URL a user is redirected to following JWT validation

    • this attribute is useful for handling deeplinking

    • as the request comes from a trusted source Workvivo's JWT Consumer does not verify the authenticity of the URL

    • optional

  • mobile

    • boolean

    • a value of true allows Workvivo to respond using a Mobile "Claimed URL".

    • For mobile devices, it is important to set the JWT mobile attribute, if not then Workvivo native mobile application will NOT launch.

    • optional

  • third_party_id

    • a string, max length 191

    • this is a private claim / custom claim

    • identifies the user as per customer’s standard, which might be the users email.

    • optional - however, one of the following is required: email, third_party_id, workvivo_id

  • workvivo_id

    • an integer

    • this is a private claim / custom claim

    • identifies the user as per Workvivo standard

    • optional - however, one of the following is required: email, third_party_id, workvivo_id

  • email

    • this is a private claim / custom claim

    • identifies the user via their email address

    • optional - however, one of the following is required: email, third_party_id, workvivo_id

  • Note that one of following is mandatory in order to identify the individual.

    • third_party_id

    • workvivo_id

    • email

item.description:
For a detailed and in-depth explanation of JWT SSO see the following documentation. For configuration settings see this demonstration walk through. You can also review configuration settings in the following documentation.

Required Headers

Headers for JWT SSO are different to other APIs. There is no requirement for the Authorization Bearer token. The following two headers are required.

  • organisation-id: Your Workvivo Organisation ID. You can find this in Workvivo in Apps Settings

  • x-workvivo-jwt: Your generated JWT

Important Notes

  • URL

    • Base URL is NOT https://api.workvivo.com instead it is https://[your workvivo domain]/

    • The end point is not prefixed with /api/.. it is /proxy/redirect/sso

    • Full URL would look like https://[your workvivo domain]/proxy/redirect/sso e.g. https://acme.workvivo.com/proxy/redirect/sso

  • Mobile

    • The JWT Claim / attribute mobile should to set to true. This allows Workvivo to respond using a Mobile "Claimed URL". It's important to set the JWT mobile attribute, if not then Workvivo native mobile application will NOT launch.

  • CORS (Cross Origin Resource Sharing)

    • The above demonstration walk through mentions and demonstrates CORS. It's likely you will encounter CORS, it's recommended to review the demonistration walk through.

    • To cater for CORS its important to configure allowed origins within the Workvivo JWT SSO settings.

  • Javascript Sample Code

    • Sample Javascript code is provided here

    • This sample JS code uses a fetch command to send the JWT to Workvivo

  • Permissions

    • the Role IT Administratoris required to configure JWT SSO settings
